title: REDEFINES — same bytes interpreted as both numeric and alphanumeric
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. CLAIM-CLASSIFY.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-CLAIM-REC.
           05  WS-CLAIM-AMT-NUM    PIC 9(7)V99.
           05  WS-CLAIM-AMT-TXT    REDEFINES WS-CLAIM-AMT-NUM
                                   PIC X(9).
           05  WS-CLAIM-STATUS     PIC X.
      *> REDEFINES overlays WS-CLAIM-AMT-TXT on the same 9 bytes as
      *> WS-CLAIM-AMT-NUM. The program writes the numeric, then reads
      *> the same bytes as text to log a denormalised audit string.
      *> Reordering the fields, or treating them as independent
      *> properties in a modern record type, BREAKS the contract.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           MOVE 1234567.89 TO WS-CLAIM-AMT-NUM
           DISPLAY "Raw bytes were: " WS-CLAIM-AMT-TXT
           STOP RUN.
notes:
REDEFINES is the COBOL counterpart to Fortran EQUIVALENCE: two
field names share the same storage. A naive Java/C# port that
maps each name to an independent property silently drops the
overlay. The spec must flag the storage sharing AND surface
encoding/USAGE as an open question -- the visible bytes depend
on whether AMT-NUM is DISPLAY (zoned-decimal ASCII/EBCDIC) or
COMP-3 (packed). Calibrated against insurance-batch and banking-
sample COBOL programs where REDEFINES is used as an audit-
rendering hack.
